# New volunteer training weekend agenda

The volunteer training weekend is scheduled for the first weekend of April, covering both theoretical knowledge and hands-on experience with the weather station network. This agenda covers the core competencies needed for routine maintenance visits and basic troubleshooting, with practical sessions at accessible stations to build confidence before volunteers take on independent site visits.

## Saturday morning: Network overview and safety

**9:00-9:30 - Welcome and introductions**
Coffee and brief introductions for new volunteers, with current volunteers sharing experience of different sites and common issues they've encountered. This informal session helps match new volunteers with experienced buddies for their first few independent visits.

**9:30-10:30 - Network layout and station roles**
Overview of the fourteen active stations, their locations, and why each was positioned where it is. Map work covering access routes, terrain challenges, and which stations can be reached by vehicle versus on foot. Discussion of the data each station type collects and how it fits into the broader valley weather picture.

**10:30-11:00 - Safety protocols and emergency procedures**
Weather conditions that make site visits unsafe, particularly around AWS-09 and AWS-14 where terrain is challenging. Mobile phone coverage map and designated check-in times for remote site visits. Basic first aid review and when to abandon a maintenance visit if conditions deteriorate.

**11:00-12:00 - Tool familiarization and equipment check**
Hands-on introduction to the standard toolkit: multimeter, torque wrench, spare batteries, basic hand tools. How to test battery voltage under load, when readings indicate replacement is needed, and proper handling of sealed lead-acid batteries. Equipment sign-out procedures and responsibility for returning kit in good condition.

## Saturday afternoon: Hands-on station work

**13:00-15:00 - Live station maintenance at AWS-05**
Practical session at the road-accessible AWS-05 covering routine maintenance tasks: visual inspection checklist, rain gauge calibration check, antenna integrity verification, and battery voltage testing. Each new volunteer performs these tasks under supervision with the standard toolkit.

**15:00-16:00 - Data logger interaction and troubleshooting**
How to interpret the status LED patterns, when to power-cycle a logger, and what information to record on station cards. Common problems and their field solutions: loose connections, water ingress indicators, and antenna issues. What constitutes an emergency requiring immediate attention versus problems that can wait for the next scheduled visit.

**16:00-17:00 - Radio signal testing and LoRa basics**
Using handheld radios to verify signal paths, interpretation of signal strength readings, and understanding of duty cycle limitations. Basic LoRa network concepts without excessive technical detail, focusing on why transmission intervals matter and how multiple stations share the same frequency band.

## Sunday morning: Advanced topics and commissioning

**9:00-10:00 - Enclosure modifications and waterproofing**
Current efforts to resolve water ingress issues, including the venting trials and desiccant placement experiments. How to identify moisture problems early and temporary fixes that can be applied during routine visits while permanent solutions are developed.

**10:00-11:30 - New station commissioning process**
Step-by-step walkthrough of installing a new weather station, from site selection through initial data validation. This session is primarily observational since new installations are rare, but gives volunteers the background to assist with commissioning when opportunities arise.

**11:30-12:00 - Seasonal variations and planning**
How maintenance requirements change through the year, winter access limitations, and the increased battery replacement frequency during low-light periods. Planning visits around weather windows and why some stations require more frequent attention than others.

## Sunday afternoon: Documentation and reporting

**13:00-14:00 - Paperwork and record keeping**
Proper completion of station cards, when to escalate issues through the group chat versus handling them independently, and how maintenance records inform long-term network planning. Examples of good and poor documentation from past visits.

**14:00-15:00 - Dashboard interpretation and data quality**
Reading the network dashboard, identifying data anomalies that warrant site visits, and understanding normal versus concerning patterns in sensor readings. How to correlate weather events with station performance issues.

**15:00-16:00 - Questions, buddy system assignment, and first visit planning**
Open discussion for specific questions about individual stations or procedures. Assignment of new volunteers to experienced buddies for their first independent visits, with scheduling of those initial paired visits before the weather turns properly warm and some access routes become overgrown.

## Equipment allocation for training

Each new volunteer will be issued a basic toolkit during the training weekend, consisting of a digital multimeter, basic hand tools, spare fuses, and a handheld radio programmed with network frequencies. Battery replacement tools and spare batteries remain centrally managed and are checked out only for specific maintenance visits.

The training weekend toolkit includes demonstration batteries in various states of charge to practice voltage testing without affecting operational equipment, plus a disassembled rain gauge mechanism for hands-on calibration practice without disrupting data collection from active stations.
